:::{#cor-cross-entropy-entropy}
#### Entropy is the cross-entropy of a distribution with itself

Let $X$ be a [discrete random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-discrete-rv) with [probability mass function](random-variables.qmd#def-pmf) $p$ on $\set{1, \ldots, K}$.
Then

$$H(p, p) = \entropyf{X}.$$

:::

::: proof

By @thm-cross-entropy-expectation with $q = p$, $H(p, p) = \E{-\log p_X}$.
Since $\P(X = k) = p_k$, the [random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-random-variable) $-\log p_X$ is the [surprisal](#def-surprisal) $\surprisalf{X}$.
This is finite with [probability](probability-basics.qmd#def-probability) 1, because $X$ takes only values with $p_k > 0$,
and the values with $p_k = 0$ contribute $0$ to both $H(p, p)$ and $\entropyf{X}$ by the convention in their definitions.
So $H(p, p) = \E{\surprisalf{X}} = \entropyf{X}$ by the definition of [entropy](#def-entropy).

:::
